notes.title: Early Access: Update 9, Patch 1 – Class & Combat Bug Fixing
notes.notes:
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44237228/5a52afcf87e2f6f505624be525fb0ea7d6d6072b.png"]Greetings, Aces!

This patch sharpens your swings, steadies your perks, and squashes some pesky bugs … Launcher behavior is tighter, Focus gains are smoother, and issues—like revive hiccups, UI oddities, and Request Board mix-ups—have been cleaned up.

Check out details below. As always, your feedback helps shape these updates—keep it coming!
[hr][/hr]Combat & Gameplay
Combat HUD

Fixed instances of the Combat Mini HUD disappearing when performing certain actions (drinking a Flask, using a Focus Skill, using an Umbra, etc)

Fixed an issue where the enemy’s healthbar would animate smoothly when attacked (this now behaves the way that it used to prior to Update 9)

Fixed an issue where the player can start/skip part of the revive process before the pop-up appears

Boomguard Legacy

Fixed an issue that caused Boomguard Legacy’s perk to not work with the Rockbreaker universal launcher attack.

Adjusted the launch trajectory of the explosion so that it’s easier to do combos.

Adjusted the launch timing so that it’s easier to perform follow up combos.

Request Board

Fixed an issue where an incorrect number of Launchers were required to complete the Ready to Launch request.

Classes & Allies
Sentinel

Heavy Combo Finisher (HHH) is now considered a launcher and should work in conjunction with perks like Boomguard’s Legacy

Explosion from Sanguine Burst no longer knocks enemies far away and now applies the same type of launch opportunities as the normal HHH combo finisher

Shadowstriker

Meter gain from basic attacks have been slightly improved to accommodate for the recent fixes to Focus Meter gain from certain perks. 

McKraken

Fixed an issue where Atoll Oasis Focus Meter gain effect did not work if the Ace was in air

Ryx

Fixed an issue that caused Ryx to remain stationary in missions if the Ace teleports to other party members

Fixed an issue where Ryx does not join the player to fight the Gobo Impaletail in the Snaggleshire Venture

notes.title: Early Access: Update 9 - New! Community Requests
notes.notes:
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44237228/561461f61b71d0cf33869d1b725b489ba14edcf1.png"]Greetings, Aces!

In addition to a suite of class, combat, and enemy tweaks, we’ve got some new things for you to try in this update—starting with a brand-new system we’re calling Community Requests, plus a major refresh to how you earn Writs throughout the game.

New Feature! Community Requests: Community Requests are now live! These time-limited challenges invite all Aces to contribute toward a shared goal. Each request includes personal objectives for you to tackle on your own, plus large-scale Belfry-wide milestones. 

You’ll find Community Requests in the Request Board in the Tower under the new Community tab. The first event, Rakentague Overflow, focuses on Grasslands missions, Beastkin, and Bloodletters … more detail below! 

Writ Reward Updates: We’ve fine-tuned how Writs are earned across early missions and the Job Board to help smooth out the path for new and returning Aces. More on Writs and in-game economy soon ... for now, here's what you can expect with this update. 

For rookie Aces just stepping into Towerborne, the early game grind has been lightened to get you moving faster.

Several early missions now reward 400 Writs (up from 250)

Job Board tasks now scale from 80 to 160 Writs based on difficulty. 

Requests have also been made more flexible—no need to hunt down one exact Venture anymore; now you can take on any Venture and still make progress. 

The Bell questline has been refreshed - complete it again to earn extra Writs.

Check out update details, below.
[hr][/hr]New Feature! Community Requests 
Community Request: Rakentague Overflow

A tide of enemies is coming from the Rakentague area. The Council has deemed this threat to be Ace Level, and bounties are issued. Help protect the refugees in the area! 

Community Requests are a new feature added to Towerborne in this update. This is a 3 week challenge. Each step unlocks automatically after the step before it is completed. Work together as a Community to complete the new Request to claim rewards!

Ace Goals
[olist]
Complete 5 missions in Grasslands

Defeat 200 Beastkin

Complete the Rakentague Venture
[/olist]
Belfry Goals
[olist]
Complete 1000 missions in Grasslands

Defeat 10000 Beastkin

Defeat 1000 Ratslasher Bloodletters
[/olist]
Community Requests can be found in the Request Board located in the Tower. Tab over to the Community section to see the new additions to the board. Rewards can be claimed at the board (for each step). At the end of the event, you’ll be sent unclaimed rewards automatically via in-game mail. 

Beastkin

The revive co-op experience in particular has received an overhaul which should alleviate frustrating moments. Combat also has received a substantial number of changes that will make things feel better across the board. Some of the changes are subtle but they all add up to make something that feels a lot more consistent.

The revive meter now decays over time instead of resetting when revive is canceled

It is now possible for multiple Aces to revive a downed player, which also increases how fast it takes to revive players

Gear Updates to account for Death / Revive changes

Ace Stats

Heavy -> Light combo tree has been improved significantly

Increased the amount of Weapon Meter generated from attacks

Pyroclast

Improved gameplay feel of all attacks.

Heavy -> Light combo tree has been improved

Fixed an issue that caused Jump Heavy Attack to cancel early when performed right before landing on the ground

Adjusted attack speed of the Launcher follow up blasts so that they are faster and snappier, making it easier to use

Fixed an issue where Blazing Roar did not cause Burn when the Ironflower Legendary is equipped

notes.notes:
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44237228/b8ebaee7ee8697811556e56a4dd0ee95bc679f82.png"]

Greetings, Aces!

We’ve tightened up combat, gear, and gobos alike to keep every swing, slash, and setting feeling just right. Today’s patch is all about precision—cleaner status effects, smarter enemies, and quality-of-life tweaks that make Towerborne run smoother while we cook up the next big thing.

Shipping these fixes ended up causing some other issues ... as of now, Loot Rush wrapped a week earlier than planned—for those dodge-roll hungry Aces scooping up shinys, our humblest apologies for the rug-pull! We know that caught some of you mid-run, but please know that we’ll be leveling up systems across the board.

No matter what - your feedback on any Limited-Time Mode, or anything for that matter - drives our next steps; keep it coming! 

[hr][/hr]Classes & Combat
Class Skills

Sentinel

Fixed an issue that caused bleed from Prickly Strikes received from Sanguine Assault to only lasts for 2 seconds instead of 4 seconds

Fixed an issue that caused Sanguine Assault to activate after exploding 6 stacks of bleed instead of 5

Fixed an issue that caused Bleed inflicted by Shield Surf to last 3 seconds instead of 4 seconds

Pyroclast

Fixed an issue that caused Stable Footing to not provide Stability for the correct duration

Rockbreaker

Enemies

Gobo Tormentor

notes.title: Early Access: Update 8 - Echoes of Gratitude
notes.notes:
[img src="https://clan.fastly.steamstatic.com/images//44237228/25a69c519461beb2773d930548c3baf5359983d3.png"]Greetings, Aces!

From the moment Towerborne hit Early Access last September—and through April’s game-shaping update—you’ve been with us every swing of the Warclub. You’ve toppled titans, lit up Umbra Shrines, leveled classes, and traded war stories in the Belfry. We set out to build a game we wanted to play, and we knew it would only reach its full potential with you right beside us.

That spirit fuels our latest (massive) update-celebration, Echoes of Gratitude. From bug-hunting to every “hey, what if…?” our Founders - those Aces who've played with us on our road to 1.0 launch - have helped sculpted Towerborne into what it is today, and like any good squad-mate, we've got your back!
Update 8 Overview
With this update, expect a bigger world and a deeper game, including a new Danger Level 5 zone, new Ventures, new Chance Encounters, new enemies and a new Umbra - and more. Quality of life improvements include early runs feeling smoother, fewer pop-ups, a rebalanced DL 2 trial, cleaner mission flow, and more.  
[previewyoutube="FZ5NQCpDY6w;full"][/previewyoutube]Echoes of Gratitude Celebration
To show our thanks, we’re throwing the Belfry doors wide open for a week of Free Play Days! Yes, it’s exactly like it sounds … play for free on Steam (June 11–18) or Xbox (June 12–18) - these Free Play Days serve two purposes: first, a big thank-you! And second, they’ll help us test our systems to make sure we ship the best possible game when we officially launch - for everyone! Beyond that, we’ve lined up a slate of in game (and out-of-game) goodies – see the full list below!

Give it all a whirl and - as always - we can’t wait to hear what you think.

__________
Echoes of Gratitude
We hope all of what we’ve got in store resonates with you - each item below is a version of our way of saying - thank you for suiting up alongside us!
Jump Into Free Play Days! (limited time)
Towerborne will be free to play on Steam (June 11-18) and Xbox (June 12-18). No codes. No hoops. Just jump in and play! Couch co-op just got a bit cozier. Founders with those laggard pals - have them join the squad! Additionally, Towerborne is on sale across platforms (for a limited time) - if you’ve been waiting to become a Founder yourself, this is a great time to do it.

[img src="https://clan.fastly.steamstatic.com/images//44237228/8ad81329c3ae816dce7812b6a74652842d434bd9.jpg"]
Update 8 is Here!
We are building Towerborne to grow and evolve over time. In just the months leading up to our launch, we can probably say that we've grown significantly. And, with your continued input and feedback - we plan to keep it rolling. Update 8 is a big step in converting feedback into meaningful changes, including: combat tuning, UX polish, and measurable balance changes that we feel will improve the overall experience. Check out the details, below!

[img src="https://clan.fastly.steamstatic.com/images//44237228/5fd5ee21e6e6a35b8ffe634d4814f1785a52d5bb.png"]
New: Discord Quests!
We partnered with Discord for a special limited-time Quest. From June 11 to June 18, completing the Quest while playing Towerborne will unlock an exclusive Shiro avatar to use on Discord. 

Go here to grab the Quest via Discord! 

For a primer on how Discord Quests work, go here. 

This reward is available to all players on Steam and Xbox.
[previewyoutube="EeAdALHihIc;full"][/previewyoutube]Curio Favorites Return for a Limited Time!
Shiro’s Stash was originally set to rotate out a month ago – but thanks to the support from the community, we’ve extended the window through June 18! We’re also bringing back two fan-favorite Curios. The originally event-timed Nightcloak’s Vault and the Glacial Hoard Curio are making an appearance for a limited time. Grab these iconic cosmetics before they cycle out!

[img src="https://clan.fastly.steamstatic.com/images//44237228/db887d064005e3abff1900504abbc8d0b929fbe7.png"]
Twitch Drops: Final Chance, Full Unlock
We are so thankful to all the creators who have streamed Towerborne and to everyone who has watched and supported the game along the way. This current week (June 11-18) is also your chance to scoop up a full Twitch Drop gear set … take that, FOMO! For more details on how to participate - go here. 

[img src="https://clan.fastly.steamstatic.com/images//44237228/bec3ab22ef12cf5f51f8848d3bb64e5325dca16e.png"]
New! Belfry Heroes Wallpaper
What’s that you say? The art of Towerborne is so compelling you want it plastered across your screens?! Don’t worry, we got you! We’re keeping it going with a brand-new Heroes of the Belfry wallpaper set in full 4K resolution. All of our wallpaper, old and new, you can find here!



[img src="https://clan.fastly.steamstatic.com/images//44237228/491c454dcd246067afd770bb065030cfca4f95ce.jpg"]
Gratitude = Prizes
Two Umbra. Two cozy blankets. One lucky winner … Which one of your skilled lucky Aces will conquer this Sweepstakes-Shrine?! Enter the contest here (runners up will get their hands on either 2,000 Belfry Bucks or a Curio Core! Open to US Residents, only). 

[img src="https://clan.fastly.steamstatic.com/images//44237228/ba0590dcfed5fb6cc3dc787be4be3b1f5eb66869.png"]
[hr][/hr]Update 8 Details
A stiff breeze is rolling in from the mountains … and along with it, a fresh zone for Danger Levels 4 and 5, new Ventures, new Chance Encounters, and a new enemy to test your mettle too. There is more game to play and world to explore - and you'll have a better time  doing it. This update also delivers relatively smoother runs overall. New players have a faster experience learning the game—fewer pop-ups, a rebalanced License 2 trial, and better mission-to-mission flow. Couch co-op squads now share quest steps while everyone hunts for new Legendary weapons, gear sets – and last but not least, a new Umbra ally to join your fight. 

Here are the details:
Gameplay & Exploration


[img src="https://clan.fastly.steamstatic.com/images//44237228/26a58792f38e675945113698f527134690b87d98.png"]

Greetings, Aces!

Greetings (and welcome!), Aces! 

Today, rookie Aces join the ranks - because New Class Skills, Cross-play, Cross Progression, and Console Couch Co-Op (Xbox only) are all here! All at once!

[previewyoutube=dez6x0vFqiw;full][/previewyoutube] 

New and deeper gameplay is here alongside our Xbox Game Preview debut—so whether you’ve been brawling since Steam Early Access or you’re hopping in on Game Pass, you’ll find deeper progression, more ways to play, and couch co-op on console (only on console for now) for the first time. 

With the new Class Skills system, we’re also delivering a special Limited Time Event: Shiro’s Golden Journey. And hey, if you want to give your thumbs a break from all the Gobo bashing button mashing, why not sit back and flip on a Towerborne Twitch stream so you can grab yourself a Twitch Drop or two, too… 

While every player has a full gameplay loop at their fingertips - Towerborne is still in Steam Early Access and Xbox Game Preview; but so far, on our road to the 1.0 launch, we’ve fielded fantastic feedback from our Founders - those of you who’ve chosen to commit to playing and building with us. Keep it coming. Hit us up on Discord. And let’s keep redefining looter brawlers, together. New Class Skills Introducing the Class Skills Progression System! As you level up your Class, unlock a huge variety of Skills across 5 categories: Focus Skills, Weapon Mechanic, Moveset, Advanced Combat, and Support. Spend Skill Points to Equip or Unequip Skills on the fly (provided you have the points), allowing for deep customization. Mix and match skills and weapons, blend builds with certain combat tactics for different results. Craft a build that truly suits your playstyle! {STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44237228/5b24125797f214d08fcec51efbbcf1838e8f32aa.png Legendary LootPrepare for the hunt! We've added new Legendary Weapons for every class and new Legendary Gear items, dropping in Danger Level 5 content, including specific items from Boss Lairs. The powerful Boomguard's set also joins the DL5 loot pool. We've updated substats on many existing Legendaries, adjusted how rarity impacts Class Level requirements, and revamped Aspects – there are now 3 types (Helm, Chest, Weapon) you can equip 1 of each, changing build possibilities (note: Leg items no longer have Aspect slots). Some overly common Legendaries are now rarer. World Map, ReimaginedThe entire World Map has been reimagined for better flow and variety. Discover new Chance Encounters, now with custom map art hinting at their contents and deeper ties to nearby Ventures. Explore updated Venture Danger Levels, tackle the new Mossbosk Venture at DL 5, experience adjusted narratives in areas like the Backhills, and meet two new Umbra: Boshi and Querida! Ace XP rewards for exploration have also been rebalanced and generally increased.{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44237228/b67e617eaca5c4ce923c0c28e79d5e67f9178329.png Gameplay & Quality of Life UpdatesWe've smoothed out gameplay with fixes like improved input buffering (making air attacks after jump cancels more reliable), adjusted Universal Block Break to be faster and allow Jump Cancels, made Powderkeg Punch cancels more reliable, and tweaked Shadow Feint activation. Interact directly with players in the Tower or on the World Map to group up, view profiles, or add friends – including cross-platform Stoic Friends! You can also now participate in Towerborne Twitch drop campaigns and link your Steam and Xbox accounts.The DetailsWhen it comes to new skill trees (for each class) and a whole lot of map and missions to explore and conquer ... the devil is in more than just the details, it's in playing the game. You'll find a detailed breakdown below of what this update has to offer. But the real magic happens when you feel it come together amongst your friends and foes out in the field of battle. More requests are available. Players will see a guaranteed variety of requests daily. Four requests will be available daily instead of three.  During certain events/activities, more requests will be made available, e.g. Golden Week.  Request rewards have been adjusted.  Combat & Classes The Class Skills system adds a whole new world of possibilities to each Class. It’s up to you to pick and choose your Skills in a way that best suits your playstyle.  Class Skills Progression System  One of the biggest changes to combat comes in the form of Class Skills. This new progression mechanic aims to provide players with a large variety of choice and customization options that unlock as you level up your Classes. Each Skill has a Skill Point Cost associated with it. However, spending points is not a permanent action. You are able to Equip or Unequip Skills however you like, provided you have enough points to do so. There are five main categories to customize: Focus Skills, Weapon Mechanic, Moveset, Advanced Combat, and Support.  New! The Mender’s Flask  The concept of Lives has been removed from the game. It is now replaced by the Mender’s Flask. Pressing Up on the d-pad will allow the Ace to heal 40% of your health. In solo play, reaching zero health will now result in Defeat.  It will be possible to improve various aspects of Healing as you progress through the game.  By default, the max number of Mender’s Flasks is 1. Interacting with a Shrine refills the Mender’s Flask by 1. Defeating LTs provides a guaranteed Mender’s Flask drop.  Run towards the Flask to pick it up.   Focus Skills are no longer locked to specific weapons. Instead, Focus Skills are unlocked via leveling up the Class of your choice. This means it’s now possible to mix and match your favorite Light and Heavy Focus Skills! Weapon Mechanics have been greatly expanded thanks to the new Skill system. Some of the new Skills provide small tweaks or improvements to existing mechanics, while others provide all new opportunities that drastically change the way you play. The Ace’s Standard Moveset can also be expanded with new Skills. You’ll be able to perform air evades, recover quickly when launched, or even perform wake up attacks after being knocked down. Advanced Combat is where you add new moves, modify existing moves, or apply unique perks to your Class. Some of these are pretty wild, so please look forward to checking them all out! The Support category is where you can modify your Class to do things that help you when times are tough. Need more Mender’s Flasks? Want to help heal your party? Want to survive a devastating attack that normally would lead to defeat?  General Due to the new Class Skill system, there are a lot of changes under the hood that may not be listed here. Instead, some of the bigger highlights will be shared. However, it’s worth noting that general gameplay should feel much improved even if it’s not specifically called out.  Fixed an issue across all gameplay that prevented inputs from being buffered correctly when pressed very quickly. This should result in air attacks to be performed more reliably after jump canceling an Evade. Rising Recovery is now a Skill that unlocks at Level 5. This action allows you to quickly rise from the ground by pressing Jump or Evade. Universal Launchers are now gated by Skill progression and unlocks at Level 7. Focus Meter gain, Weapon Meter gain, and Break Bar damage has been rebalanced across the board for all 4 Classes.  Class Updates  Sentinel  Valor has been redesigned  Valor now becomes available at Level 8 Valor is now activated by pressing LT+RB (or C on Keyboard)  The following Skills can now be performed while airborne. These attacks also reset your combo counter, allowing you to perform more airborne attacks! Updated the Tower Guard player companion so they have their own move set with three attacks and a unique weapon. Enemies will not perform any evades or wake-up attacks until DL 3 and above. Fixed various bugs that resulted in enemies being put into an unresponsive state when blocking or having their Break Bar broken at specific moments in gameplay.  Enrage Adjustments  Red visual tells have been added to enemies about to Enrage to signify that an Unblockable Attack is about to occur. Greetings, Aces!

While we continue to get after it to build bigger and better – we’re keeping the ball rolling in this small-but-mighty update with cleaner combat, sharper balance, and a few pesky bugs retired. Enemy attacks are a little fairer, abilities feel a little snappier, and your gear should be working just the way it should.

This update might look smaller on the surface, but it’s laying the groundwork for what’s next. Most of the player-facing changes are about tuning and fixes, but behind the scenes, Update 5 is doing a lot of heavy lifting. Without it, some of the bigger things we’ve got in the pipeline wouldn’t be possible. So hang in there—we’ve got more coming soon, and we think you’re going to be excited about what’s next.

In the meantime, check out this update’s deets, below!

… and, later this month - we've got a cool new mode built to test your strength and skills and most of all - speed. We’re putting the finishing touches on it as we speak…just needs a little more time⏳ 

[hr][/hr]
Gameplay & Exploration
This update keeps things running smoother with balance tweaks, tuning, and groundwork for what's next—setting the stage for future content.

Items
    
    Somewhat increased base ATK and DEF values when upgrading items past Level 50.
    Exploding Mushroom hazards dropped by The Fumigator legendary now have different coloring than normal Exploding Mushroom hazards.
    Fixed a bug with Wildling’s Sword where it now drops with the correct Focus Gain stat.
    Feral’s Bane legendary daggers will now drop with the ATK stat instead of DEF stat. Only applies to items acquired post-update.
    The Northern Inferno legendary warclub will now drop with the Weapon Meter Gain stat instead of Burn Resistance. Only applies to items acquired post-update.
    Settings Update
    
    Player settings preferences are now linked to accounts rather than devices.
    Job Board
    
    Job board quests requiring players to play missions with a specific Umbra equipped now require players to use specific Umbra skills during missions.
    Combat
This update fine-tunes combat across the board—smoother attacks, better responsiveness, and adjustments that make every fight feel tighter and more fluid.
Classes

Rockbreaker
    
    YXXX Combo Finisher now hits 13 frames earlier.
    Shadowstriker
    
    Fixed an issue where the Dash Light Combo Finisher was missing a Dodge Cancel window.
    Pyroclast
    
    Various improvements to the feel of attacks. In general, attacks should still feel weighty but are technically faster than before. It’s largely subtle but it makes a difference!
    Umbra

McKraken
    
    Adjusted animation start-up time so that it feels more in line with other Umbra.
    Increased Focus Meter generation rate… have fun!
    Morberry
    
    Adjusted animation start-up time so that it feels more in line with other Umbra.
     Enemies

General
    
    Visual tells have been improved for a variety of enemies. Many Lieutenants now have added recovery tells or start-up tells for their unique attacks.
    Visual improvements have been made to the Break Bar recovery moment. Enemies have more obvious tells before the burst occurs.
    Ratslasher
    
    Added a visual tell to the 3rd hit of its combo chain so that it’s easier to identify that it block breaks and that it’s not a true combo.
    This is an attack that is meant to be evaded midway through even on hit. This moment should be more obvious now.
    Quivertail
    
    Adjusted hitboxes on Opportunity Attack so that it better matches the visual of the animation.

notes.title: Early Access: Update 4 - New Missions & Languages
notes.notes:
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44237228/ba7780266fa7bdbbcf335543e5ff2eb1404d6c7a.png
Greetings, Aces!

Happy 2025! Our first update of the year is here—bringing exciting new updates, including mission types and map improvements, expanded language support, and a special perk for Founders: the ability to claim all previous Monthly Bonuses.

Kicking things off, the World Map will feature three new mission types. Each can be completed once, and some have graduated from discovery tiles to permanent spots on the map. Beyond that, we’ve fine-tuned combat and enemy behaviors, and polished up the visuals (no more NPCs mysteriously losing their faces—oops!). Enemies now have sharper responses and clearer tells, making fights challenging but fair. Plus, this update brings some love to your inventory, tweaks to item stats, and improved mission flow to keep things moving.

What’s that you say? More-monster-mangling was your New Year’s Resolution, too?! Well, then—what are you waiting for? Ready up, Aces … this year is gonna be a doozy.

[hr][/hr]
More Languages
The Belfry continues to welcome Aces from around the world with these new options, bringing our support language count to 23:

Polish (pl-PL)
Danish (da-DK)
Swedish (sv-SE)
Norwegian (nb-NO)
Finnish (fi-FI)
Gameplay & Exploration
This update hits some quality-of-life love for your inventory, item balancing fun, tweaks to mission and progression flow, and more. Dive in and see what’s new!

Founders: Claim Past Monthly Bonuses!

With this update, Founders can now claim all previous Monthly Founder Bonuses—no more Ace envy for you newer Aces out there!
New Mission Types
Three new types of missions can be found on the World Map. Each one of these missions can be completed once. Some of these missions used to appear in discovery tiles, but now have a permanent location on the map. These were missions like escorting the wagon or helping the City of Number refugees as they try to make their way to the Belfry.

Guide and Guard - Protect or escort wagons.
Bait and Clear - New challenging missions where players progress through waves of enemies by ringing a bell.
Chance Encounter - Unique experiences for the Ace to discover (Some of these you may have come across in a discovery mission before, but there are also new encounters and missions to discover).
Quality of Life Improvements
Easier Group Finder Access

You now don’t have to go back to the Belfry to access Group Finder; find your group from the World Map, too! 
Storage Increase

Increased the Aspect inventory storage limit from 50 to 80, to match the Weapon and Gear storage limits.
Loot Adjustments

Improved the drop rates for many Legendary items that were rarer than intended.
Adjusted loot throughout the game to bias slightly in favor of gear dropping over weapons.
Item Stats Balance

Strike DMG min/max random substat values reduced.
Umbra Strength min/max random substat values increased.
The “Focus Gain When Hit” item stat is now considered a Legacy stat. It will still function on existing items with this stat, but will no longer appear on newly acquired items.
Its functionality has been rolled into the “Focus Gain on Hit” stat, which has now been relabeled to “Focus Gain.”
Changed the static substats of the “Cambulary’s Strength” Legendary Sword:
   
   Bleed DMG → DMG Reduction
   Crit DMG → Strike DMG
   Existing Cambulary’s Strength items will be considered legacy items and retain their original affixes.
   Changed one of the static substats of the “Red Handed” Legendary Gauntlets:
   
   Crit DMG → Health Per Hit
Existing Red Handed items will be considered legacy items and retain their original affixes.
   Crit DMG is now calculated as a multiplicative modifier rather than additive. It will now stack as expected with other damage modifiers like Strike DMG.

Tech Tweaks

You can now scan a unique QR code in the Settings Menu to reach the ticket submission page to receive support.
Various network stability fixes.
Improved framerate while navigating menus.
Fixed an issue with incorrect player profiles being shown.
Mission & Progression Adjustments

The conversation screen that displayed “I don’t have anything for you right now” has been removed. The screen will now close if an NPC doesn’t have any new conversations. If you interact with an NPC that doesn’t have any conversations, a menu will display indicating no conversations are available.
After loading into a mission, the quest tracker now hides itself after a couple of seconds. The information can still be brought back up by pressing 2 on the keyboard or RIGHT arrow on controller.
Fixed a bug with Danger License Trials not displaying health bars correctly, and reinforcement enemies not spawning.
Adjustments have been made to how encounters are selected in discovery missions, resulting in a more varied experience.
Discovery missions now have a more contained selection of enemies.
Numbers Ironworks background art was updated.
Combat
Classes

Sentinel: Fixed an issue where certain Combo Finishers were not tagged properly.
Pyroclast: Fixed an issue where certain Combo Finishers were not tagged properly.
Rockbreaker:
   
   Fixed an issue that caused a Level 1 Powderkeg Punch to hit later than expected.
   Fixed an issue that caused a Level 3 Powderkeg Punch to fire automatically while charging when paired with certain Aspects.
   Adjusted the visual language of Skyward Swing’s vortex to improve gameplay visibility.
   Shadowstriker:
   
   Fixed an issue that caused Sunrise Shrapnel to have a smaller hitbox than intended.
   Adjusted the hitbox on Dash Light Attack so that it hits more reliably.
   Air Heavy Attack, when used as a Combo Finisher, is now properly counted as a Finisher.
   Umbra

Sten: Adjusted commit window so that you’re less likely to lose a charge if interrupted during the cast animation.
Picus: Fixed an issue that caused airborne enemies to not get put into the proper hit reaction.
Grimel: Adjusted cancel window timing so that you can do combos more intuitively.

Enemies
Your foes just got a little smarter—and fairer! This update polishes enemy behavior, improves visual cues, and makes fights smoother without losing the challenge.

Break Bar:
   
   Enemies now have a much more obvious animation tell when they’re about to reactivate their Break Bar after being stunned.
   Adjusted hitbox of reactivate shockwave so that it feels less sudden when it hits the Ace.
   Enrage:
   
   Enemies now have a much more obvious animation tell when they’re about to activate Enrage. Enrage now hits on frame 60 instead of frame 25.
   Lowered Break Bar HP for fodder enemies, making it easier to break them, which deactivates the Enrage state.
   
Enemy Adjustments
Flickertail:
   
   Adjusted landing frames from the Leapshot so that it’s easier to punish on whiff.
   Adjusted movement behavior to alleviate an issue where Flickertail walked backwards more often than intended.
   Adjusted the hitboxes of the Smoke Bomb projectiles so that they’re more reflective of the visual.
   Adjusted Flaming Sky Arrows so that there is a visual tell that signals their landing positions.
   Gobo Brute:
   
   Adjusted cooldowns to improve the pacing of the fight.
   Added a new attack tell to the dashing Heavy Attack so that it’s less abrupt in gameplay.
   Added missing Block Breaker warning visual to the dashing Heavy Attack.
   Adjusted the hitbox of the dashing Heavy Attack so that it better reflects the swipe visual.
   Gobo Tailwhipper:
   
   Fixed an issue that caused the Tailwhipper to not go into a proper reaction when Parried.
   Merk Marauder:
   
   The running Charge Attack has been adjusted so that it only causes a Stun when the Marauder is Enraged.
   Fixed an issue that caused the Flipping Double Axe Attack to hit earlier than intended.
   Merk Slugger & Conscript:
   
   Adjusted attack cooldowns to better pace their combat actions and alleviate frustration.
   Adjusted attack ownership so that the Ace doesn’t get put into repeated hitstun reactions in quick succession.
   Dusker Nightmare:
   
   Fixed an issue that caused Parry VFX to not appear correctly.
   Dusker:
   
   Fixed an issue that caused Parry VFX to not appear correctly.
   The Shepherd:
   
   Fixed an issue that caused Parry VFX to not appear correctly.
   Yxil:
   
   Adjusted hitboxes of ground projectiles so that it’s easier to jump over them.
   Fixed a bug that caused the Ground Stab visuals to appear underneath the ground instead of on top of the ground.
   Adjusted the timing of the stab so that it pops out from the ground 10 frames later. It also has a longer visual warning to help players anticipate the attack.
   
UI/UX
We’ve spruced up the interface so it’s smoother. Plus, we added some audio flair and squashed a few bugs—because no one likes those.

Fixed multiple danger license-related layout bugs in various languages.
Added keyboard scrolling in popups.
Improved readability of pinned quest text.
Added a warning when purchasing a cosmetic when the base item is not yet owned.
Fixed layout of Ace rank and name in the group tab.
Fixed multiple layout issues on the job board with certain combinations of languages and font sizes.
Fixed layout of challenge timer in cases where it could become obstructed.
Added an audio cue when starting a DLT.
Fixed points in the store where the scroll bar could disappear.
Fixed the mark-mode in the forge not letting players swap tabs.

Art
Bug fixing on the Art front should sharpen up your visual experience while making sure NPCs are looking their best. Enjoy!

Fixed a Z-fighting issue in the Rescue Husband Event in the Mountains Biome.
Fixed an issue where a Tower NPC was missing facial features.
Fixed an issue with Ogden’s facial features in the conversation screen.
Fixed a clipping issue with the Steamsilk Belt.
Fixed a skinning issue with the Numberian Shoulderpads.
Fixed a skinning issue with the Grandeur Guardian Belt.
Fixed a clipping issue with the Glacial Grandmaster Cape.

notes.title: Early Access: Update 3 - Grandeur
notes.notes:
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44237228/8807d60b0376c4f5f08d0dd23ad67e939f2b5f57.png

'Twas the Night Before Grandeur...

...and all through the Tower,  
Fellow Aces were stirring—hey, there’s loot to be scoured!
... for Umbra were nestled in hues rainbow-bright,  
While mistle torches burned softly, lighting up the night.  

Bumble was quiet, his thoughts far away,  
Ogden had plans to bring joy to the day.  
“Take him to the mountains!” he said with a grin,  
“To witness the light shows and let Yuletide begin!”  

With Aces prepared and Bumble in tow,  
Through snow-covered trails, they braved the wild glow.  
To a bonfire of mistle they traveled with care,  
A gift from their friends—a spark to repair.  

High in the north, where the skies softly gleam,  
Bundles are burned, inspired by a dream.  
From mistle trees' branches and secretive lore,  
Families create hues that light up the shore.  

But beware, brave Aces, for Gobos abound,  
They’ve swapped bombs for brass bells with a jingling sound.  
Don’t be fooled—yes, their chimes may delight,  
Get close, and BOOM—it’ll end your good night!  

As furnaces roar and the Belfry stands tall,  
The season of Grandeur brings warmth to us all.  
Gather your allies, your quest is near—  
‘Tis the season to conquer this festive frontier! 

[previewyoutube=0zoLdiC_PYM;full][/previewyoutube]

[hr][/hr]
The Big Picture...

Season’s Greetings, Aces! 

With this update, we’re thrilled to unveil Towerborne’s December Update, Grandeur, decking the tower-halls with a wave of holiday magic! 

Enjoy the Belfry adorned with festive decorations while you embark on a delightful quest to help Bumble rekindle his holiday spirit. Don’t forget to partake in the “12 Days of Grandeur” for daily sticker surprises. Plus, we’re excited to announce localization—Towerborne now supports 18 total languages to spread the love (and punching/stabbing/slicing/bludgeoning).  

As we continue our Early Access journey, Founder feedback remains essential in shaping Towerborne into something truly special. So please, keep the feedback coming! And in the meantime, jump into Grandeur and celebrate this festive season with us!  

Here's what to expect...

Calling All Aces … From Around the World!
As winter winds swirl and festive lights glow in every corner, Towerborne is proudly throwing its doors open to adventurers far and wide. What’s the best gift we could give this season? A chance for more heroes, from more places, to join the party!  

Beyond English, you can now immerse yourself in heroic quests, playful banter, and rich storytelling in French, Italian, Latin American Spanish, Castilian Spanish, German, Korean, Brazilian Portuguese, Portuguese, Russian, Hungarian, Czech, Dutch, Simplified Chinese, Traditional Chinese, Turkish, Japanese, and Greek. Each language adds its own spark, uniting us beneath one tower, one banner, and one grand adventure.  

And we’re just getting started! As we march ever closer to our full release, expect even more languages and greater global accessibility. Together, we’re forging a worldwide community of heroes—because the only thing better than slaying monsters and snagging epic loot is doing it side by side, no matter where you call home. Your voice, your language, your adventure—let’s take on the world together!  

A Festive Fortress
Experience the Belfry adorned with holiday-themed décor: rainbow smoke swirls from the Forge, gift boxes are tucked around every corner, and everyone’s rocking their best festive outfits. Even your Umbra buddies are sporting adorable holiday looks. It’s the perfect setting for seasonal adventures—whether it be lighting Mistle Torches or battling frustrating festive foes like Gobos tossing brass bell bombs and cold-hearted Snow Howlers.  

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44237228/404c38003fdc9b2720b70f0f0a4a3abdf4acf7c9.png

A Grand Plan
This update’s special, heartwarming quest will have you helping our favorite Forge overseer rekindle his holiday spirit. Accompany Bumble as you take a trip to the mountains—braving the rugged terrain and dodging brass bell bombs along the way. It’s times like these that the most fruitful festive-filled friendships are, well, forged. 

To start your Grandeur adventure, make sure you’ve completed the primary quest, “A Writ of Passage.” Then, head to Ogden in The Belfry at the Counsel Building to pick up the next quest, “A Grand Plan.”  

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44237228/d5f2b280dc820edc27a0e2699b62850d77643d9a.png

Holiday Cheer, Meet Holiday Gear
What’s holiday cheer without some holiday gear? Get ready for a festive arsenal of gear sets, and weapons sure to send wintery shivers down those monster spines. Here's a sneak peek at what's in store, with the full list of details in notes below.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44237228/75037806609db11e3481e128173a11a1aef4510d.png
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44237228/56450bd5cc3d80444b9549e125ab64594be21f41.png

Seasonally Sticky Daily Gifts
Join the “12 Days of Grandeur” and collect a daily surprise. Each day presents a new sticker to showcase your festive spirit in-game, adding a playful and creative touch to your character’s appearance. There are 12 stickers in all—check out a teaser of our first sticker below!  

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44237228/435356604bda9ceae1a47bf81555480d3ccd9dd4.png

[hr][/hr]
The Details...

Localization / Available Languages
Towerborne now speaks your language—literally! From the buzzing streets of Berlin to the snowy peaks of the Alps … from Tokyo’s neon nights to the bustling markets of São Paulo … and a whole bunch of places in between—we’re welcoming Aces to suit up from all over the world.  

Play in 18 languages, including English, French, Italian, Latin American Spanish, Castilian Spanish, German, Korean, Brazilian Portuguese, Portuguese, Russian, Hungarian, Czech, Dutch, Simplified Chinese, Traditional Chinese, Turkish, Japanese, and Greek. The Belfry is becoming a multi-lingual party—so pick your language, grab your controller/keyboard, and join a global adventure!

To select a preferred language, you have to change language directly within Towerborne’s in-game settings. Steam language settings do not carry over to the game.  

1. Go to Settings > Accessibility > Language.  
2. Scroll through the language options using the left or right arrow.  
3. Confirm your selection when prompted.  

Gameplay & Exploration
Get ready to deck the halls—and some Gobos—with your fists! Grandeur brings not only holiday cheer but also a slew of gameplay and exploration updates to keep every journey fresh. From a festive new questline that sends you to snowy peaks to improved loot rewards, handy new settings, and even a quick return to the Belfry, there’s something for every adventurer this season. Embrace the season with the new questline, A Grand Plan ... fire up that Grandeur bonfire … and enjoy holiday gear tweaks and the cozy feeling of a world evolving just for you!

Quality of Life & Mission Adjustments

New ‘Show Affix Roll Ranges’ Setting  
- Optionally allows the player to toggle on visibility of minimum and maximum values for randomized item stats. Found under Settings > Gameplay > General.  

Loot Adjustments  
- Increased the number of Set Bonus Venture Gear items awarded from Venture end-of-mission chests by 1.  
- Somewhat increased the amount of Writs awarded from Venture end-of-mission chests at DL 3, 4, and 5.  
- Writs will no longer drop from Venture end-of-mission chests at DL 2.  

Aspect of Dismantling Changes  
- Fixed a bug with the item name.  
- Increased the item's dismantle rewards from 80 → 140.  
- Converted the "Dismantle Me!" line into a perk, so it appears at the top of the item description in yellow text.  
- Replaced the +0 Health attribute with a randomly rolled substat.  

Quality of Life Improvements  
- Updated the introduction mission so that NPC conversations can be progressed through interacting (skip to progress).  
- Players can now travel back to the Belfry from anywhere on the World Map by using the up arrow on the D-pad or "3" on the keyboard.  

A Grand(eur) ‘Ol Time

A New Questline: A Grand Plan  
- To begin your Grandeur adventure, you must first have completed the primary quest "A Writ of Passage."  
- Once this is done, visit Ogden at the Counsel Building in The Belfry to pick up "A Grand Plan" and help bring some holiday cheer to Bumble, who is feeling homesick.  
- Earn rewards to progress the new Grandeur Event Curio!  

Aurora Ridge - New Limited-Time Venture  
- Families are looking forward to lighting the Grandeur bonfire but need to ensure it’s safe to gather.  
- The A Grand Plan quest must be completed before playing the Venture.  
- New Grandeur-themed encounters can be found throughout the game, featuring enemies like Mistle Bundle Snow Howlers and Bell-Slinging Gobos.  
- Assist travelers trying to bring presents to the Belfry and more!  

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44237228/6c94f647c393e53622a8c0bbd8b60d4eec04186c.png

Combat
Over the last few months, combat has steadily sharpened with each new update—attacks are snappier, evades flow smoother, and Classes have gained a few slick moves. In this update, we’re thrilled to introduce universal Jump Cancels, no longer limited to specific attacks! This long-awaited change clears old hurdles and opens a whole new realm of combos and strategies. While we’ll keep tweaking it over time, Jump Cancels are already in a great place. So dive in, leap into action, and enjoy the newfound freedom as you carve your path to victory!

General

Jump Cancels  
- Universally enabled Jump Cancels for all Classes from most attacks. This works similarly to the rules for Evade Cancels. If you are able to Evade Cancel an attack, then you should be able to Jump Cancel it.  
- It is now possible to Jump Cancel in any direction. For moves that had the old version of Jump Cancels, you were actually limited to jumping in a very specific way. This is no longer a limitation and should make Jump Cancels feel more intuitive.  

Jump  
- Jump now carries your momentum in ways that feel more natural than before. You may notice that your jumps will go a bit further now when moving quickly.  

Bees  
- Aces are now properly cleansed of Bees when using a Healing Shrine.  

Classes

Sentinel  
- Fixed an issue that caused Steady Strikes to not Block Break enemies as expected. This should now work consistently for all hits.  
- Fixed an issue that caused Evade/Dash Attacks to not trigger properly with Goji’s Echo equipped.  

Pyroclast

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44237228/bc9a8a7e970361f614949f14bbbc2b635913e921.png

Rockbreaker

- Improved visuals of Skyward Swing vortex.

Shadowstriker

- Fixed an issue that caused Shooting Stars to not hit grounded enemies properly.  
- Fixed an issue that caused Evade/Dash Attacks to not trigger properly with Goji’s Echo equipped.  

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44237228/326f6b9bbb36fcfcac155e31c9fdf19a59769a10.png

Enemies
For this update, the changes to enemies really revolve around quality-of-life improvements for the player. The most significant change centers around Pangojira, which will increase the challenge of this Boss in some pretty significant ways. Let us know how it feels!

Pangor  
- Fixed an issue that caused Aces to go through Pangors during their Vulnerable state.  

Quivertail

Boarealis Stoutswine

Training Room Dummy

Snow Howler

The Shepherd

The Seamstress

- Fixed an issue that allowed the Seamstress to get interrupted and launched.  
  
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44237228/8736661e397ffc735e742b78049f8ef521c07b0a.png

UI/UX
We’ve polished your interface and navigation so you can focus on the action, not the menus. Quick-hitting prompts, intuitive layouts, and subtle improvements throughout mean more time battling baddies and enjoying your winter wonderland—no compass required.

Missions and Map

notes.title: Early Access: Update 2, Patch 1 - Balancing and Bug Fixing
notes.notes:
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44237228/363eddb8f5753848df6d4210cfef5bd3095c9526.png

Gameplay & Exploration

Group Finder Works Reliably Again: Fixed an issue where canceling a search while another player joined could leave Group Finder stuck. Now, it resets properly so you can assemble your dream team without a hitch.

Gear Score Warnings Are Back: The “Recommended Gear Score” visual cue now works as intended. If you’re underpowered for a mission, you’ll see the warning in red—keeping you prepared for the fight ahead.

Smear Death Puddles Properly Animated: These hazards now animate properly after enemies are defeated, making them easier to see and dodge.

Picus Umbra Mission Timer Adjusted: Fixed an issue where the timer for this mission made it impossible for groups of four to finish.

Grimel Umbra Counts Towards Quests Now: Addressed a bug where using Grimel didn’t count for the “Me and My Umbra” quest. You can now equip Grimel and complete the quest as expected.

Combat & Classes

Focus Skills Behave as Intended: Fixed a bug where Focus Skills, meant to break enemy blocks, could be parried. These skills now function correctly, helping you dominate combat.

Powderkeg Punch Timing Clarified: There was a mix-up around the Powderkeg Punch duration for the Rock Breaker class—it was previously listed as 10 seconds, but the correct duration is actually 20 seconds.
Enemies

No More Overly Stubborn Foes: Fixed an issue that caused Yxil and Pangojira to stop taking damage when reaching specific health thresholds. Damage now occurs as expected when hitting these enemies.

notes.title: Early Access: Update 2 - Danger Level 5!
notes.notes:
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44237228/057bdd79c3bbeeaf5032aa20698fa801e9f42181.pngGreetings, Aces!

Just over two months ago, Towerborne entered Steam Early Access with 40+ hours of core gameplay, a collection of classes to conquer, gobs of gear to grind for, and bands of baddies blundering between biomes—begging to be beaten down.

Today, we’re thrilled to roll out our biggest gameplay update during early access.

We are raising the stakes with the heightened challenge of Danger Level 5—which brings dozens upon dozens more hours of gameplay that can stack up fast (depending on where you’re at in your journey and, let’s be real, just how much loot you’ve stashed). Speaking of loot, more mastery means better gear—we’re introducing the first batch of Legendary items for players to discover alongside an expanded world with over 100 new map tiles waiting to be explored.

We cherish the connection that we share with our players—and inviting all of you Founders to join us on this journey is how we keep building towards the future we talked about when we started Early Access. Of course, don’t forget that we absolutely love to show our appreciation to all of you as we continue doling out sweet Founder Bonus gear … because who doesn't love fighting and frolicking while flashing fresh Founder gear? Nobody, that's who!

We are only a couple of months into Early Access and we’ve been hard at work updating the game, and you can expect that in the weeks and months to come, we will continue this trend: Releasing new updates, sharing more information about what we're working on, and continuing to listen to your feedback. For now, know that Towerborne will keep evolving with said feedback from our Founders, forging the way forward. We’re beyond grateful to be on this journey with you and can’t wait to hear what you think about Danger Level 5 and everything that comes with it!

Here’s what’s new in this update:

NEW Group Finder (V1) ➔ We've heard your feedback on the woes of matchmaking and are introducing an early version of a Group Finder. It’s not fully functional yet - but we wanted to get something in your hands ASAP that we can build on over the coming months.
NEW Danger Level 5 ➔ Our first big content drop, expanding the map, raising the level cap to 50, and introducing tougher enemies to challenge seasoned Aces.
NEW Boss Fight: The Triumverate Awaits ➔ If you thought that Pangojira and Yxil were a threat, wait until you see what's waiting for you in the Heart of Numbers…
NEW Ventures ➔ Embark on four additional Ventures packed with formidable foes and exclusive rewards.
NEW Legendary Weapons and Gear ➔ Discover Legendary items with unique perks, adding custom power and depth to your loadout.
NEW Umbra ➔ Encounter new Umbra companions with unique abilities to aid and amplify your adventures.

[previewyoutube=aQWI-Q-xaXQ;full][/previewyoutube]
[hr][/hr]
The Big Picture
Here's a summary of the most exciting pieces of this big update. For more details, check out the section that follows.

Group Finder

The first iteration of the Group Finder is here to help connect Aces for multiple missions and varied gameplay experiences. Group leaders can advertise their groups, and players can find and automatically join groups that match their preferences. Please note that this is an early release of the Group Finder and is NOT considered FEATURE COMPLETE.

How does it work? In this first iteration of the Group Finder, we are still attempting to automatically match players together, but we've dramatically reduced the total number of pools to find people. Now, instead of waiting for more players to join you on a specific tile, you can form up a Group on the Belfry and head out to play as you wish.

Location and Danger Level options help streamline initial connections. Locations include "Any" or "Venture Farming," while Danger Levels are split into "Any," "1-3" and "4-5" to help Aces connect faster with compatible groups.
If a group is set to "Any," it will only match with other players or groups set to "Any." If a player is searching with "Any," they can match with any available group.
Players will need to remain on the Belfry while using Group Finder.
Group leaders can cancel the search at any time and start an adventure with an incomplete group if they choose.
How Is Group Finder Improving matchmaking?THIS IS JUST THE START! We needed to get this feature in your hands as quickly as possible. From here we will add more options, including the ability to see a list of groups and select the one you would like to join. Expect us to significantly increase the support of this feature over the coming months. As we expand, we plan to add options like switching between the Map and Belfry while using Group Finder and seeing a list of groups currently searching for Aces.

How can you help us? Let us know what you're using Group Finder for in the comments here on Steam, or over on Discord. Your feedback will help us determine what additional settings groups need going forward.
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44237228/d4d6f71d5025e0def90b3c419cd02e311055bb07.png
Danger Level 5

The new Danger License Trial unlocks Danger Level 5 - which includes:


Raising the level cap to 50 for a more challenging experience.
4 New Legendary Weapons, one for each class, each weapon features unique perks that add powerful options to your combat style.
12 New Legendary Gear Items: Players can equip up to 2 Legendary gear items and one legendary weapon at the same time. Legendary items will show up only at DL5.

A new chapter unfolds with the Mystweavers, bringing a fierce new battle deep within the Heart of Numbers. Prepare to face this mysterious new boss challenge by completing Ventures in DL3, DL4, and DL5.
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44237228/db5effbff5b0a8ccfa8893bb95084901e51b4a0c.pngNew Ventures & Expanded World Map

Explore more of Towerborne with an expanded world map that includes new Discovery Missions, new Ventures, new loot, new foes, and new Umbra companions exclusive to Danger Level 5. Four new Ventures await:


Numbers Ironworks: Mystweavers have taken over this industrial zone.
Silver-Gold Gates: Beastkin now control the district, preventing access.
Garrison: The Merks occupy this fort—are they working with the Mystweavers?
Heart of Numbers: The site of the City of Numbers explosion, now hosting the ultimate Mystweaver challenge.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44237228/a487b85900c17b5fe83fe3e9e6b41a01dbf625ed.jpg
New Umbra
Two new missions introduce fresh challenges and unique Umbra allies who have joined us after emerging from the mysterious depths of the Ebb...

The wise and calculating Picus has spent years navigating the veil between the Shore and Ebb; this metallic is known to be a skilled navigator adept at guiding Aces through hazardous terrain...

...or team up with Grimel – steadfast and studious, Grimel delights in lighting up dark areas and helping people look for missing items. They enjoy the smell of parchment to the point that some may find the pages of new books to be irresistibly tasty.

[previewyoutube=eBxzBDFw5nE;full][/previewyoutube]

Balancing and Quality-of-Life Enhancements

Our Danger Level 5 Update brings continued balance adjustments that refine core gameplay as new content arrives. This update introduces improvements to gear, Umbra companions, and enemies, ensuring a cohesive experience. Healing Shrines now cleanse status effects, adding a strategic edge, while expanded Aspect storage, clearer mission banners, and an optimized Forge layout make inventory and UI management smoother than ever.

The Road Ahead

Hey all, NotReallyAJedi here, I wanted to drop in and give a quick update on the promised roadmap. This one is 100% on me and I’m sorry we haven’t posted one. I know it sounds a bit cliche, but it’s been crazy since we’ve released and our primary focus has been getting things fixed, updated, created, and released for you. I have to walk back my promise here, and I’m really sorry about that. I don’t have any ETA on a roadmap for you right now.

What I CAN tell you is that our updates will continue unabated, and we have a LOT we are working on. We’ve rearranged several things in response to HOW you are playing and WHAT you are saying (hello Group Finder!), and we will continue to be as nimble and responsive as is humanly possible for a game like this.

Please forgive me for slipping on this front, but I hope that the continued updates will reassure you that we’re fervently working to make this the game you want to play!

Best,  
- NRAJ

[hr][/hr]
The Details
Here’s the breakdown of each feature and improvement in this update.

Gameplay & Exploration
Exploration & Mission Adjustments

Danger Level 5 is now available!
   
   A new Danger License Trial is available.
   The map has been expanded.
   New Quests have been added.
   New Discovery encounters, layouts, and missions have been added across all danger levels.
   2 new Umbra Shrines are now available.
   Class Level Caps increased from 40 to 50!
   4 new Venture missions are now available. (Numbers Ironworks; Numbers Garrison; Silver-Gold Gates; The Heart of Numbers)
   
New rare Legendary Weapon and Gear items to discover!
   
   4 new Legendary Weapons (1 for each class)
   12 new Legendary Gear items
   Each Legendary item has a unique perk
   You can equip 1 Legendary Weapon and up to 2 Legendary Gear items at once
   These will first begin appearing in Danger Level 5

   In general a Legendary item will have bespoke stat distribution, but the values of each of those stats will often still be variable
   
Additional new Weapon and Gear items
   
   3 new Gear Sets with Set Bonuses
   2 new Gears Sets without Set Bonuses
   6 new Venture Weapons
   
Aspect Perk Updates
   
   4 new Aspect perks that can be found on Tier 5 Aspects
   Several Aspect perks that grant a damage reduction while the player has a specific affliction have been consolidated into a single perk.
   Several Aspect perks that grant a damage bonus while the player has a specific affliction have been consolidated into a single perk.
   Several Aspect perks that grant a damage bonus while the enemy has a specific affliction have been consolidated into a single perk.
   The Aspect perk that reduces damage taken while reviving allies is now a Legacy perk and will no longer roll on newly acquired Aspects.
   The Aspect perk that reduces damage taken while airborne is now a Legacy perk and will no longer roll on newly acquired Aspects.
   Increased the Boon Duration for several Aspect perks that grant Boons (Might, Protection, etc.)
   
Balancing & Bug Fixes

Item Naming Updates
   
   Weapons, Gear, and Aspects will no longer have their item name modified by the random attributes that the item rolled (Weapons and Gear this will just result in shorter, cleaner names; Aspects will instead have their name modified based on the random perk that was assigned to the Aspect. Each perk has a unique name).
   
Item Balance
   
   Reduced roll values of the “ATK” and “DEF” item suffix substats by 20%.
   
Loot Adjustments
   
   Gear items with set bonuses will also have a small chance to drop anywhere in the world, rather than only in Venture end chests.
   Weapons that are unique to each Venture now each have a static substat, rather than all substats being fully random. This should give different weapons more flavor, and allow players to have more agency in targeting specific stats on their weapons.
   When looting a weapon, it is now weighted to be more significantly more likely to be a weapon equipable by your current class. Sentinels are more likely to loot swords, Shadowstrikers are more likely to loot daggers, etc.
   
Gear Score Adjustments
   
   Tweaked most recommended gear score values on missions. In general, recommended gear score values have been slightly increased, particularly at higher danger levels.
   
Combat
This update focuses on quality-of-life improvements across the board. Although it is possible to cancel most attacks into an Evade, there were a handful of instances where this was not true across all Classes. These scenarios have been resolved. Additionally, we found a few opportunities to improve the general feel of combat along the way.

Universally improved the feel of Dodge Roll. It is now possible to cancel the recovery frames of Dodge Rolls into attacks.
Improved the responsiveness and feel of Ground Recovery techniques when knocked down.
Fixed an issue that prevented Evade cancels if you were holding down the Focus Skill modifier button.
Changed the VFX of Might, Weakness, Protection, and Vulnerability to alleviate visual loudness when those effects are active.

In the last update, we made some significant improvements to the Sentinel Class. It’s been great seeing the positive reception to the changes. It’s definitely a bit of a teaser of things to come. For this update, a lot of the changes focus on quality-of-life improvements. notes.notes:
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44237228/86485ad2d1d6d73be54c0fe15df75e94890fcdb5.png

Greetings, Aces!

When it comes to remapping your controls - you asked, so you shall receive!

Just a day into our first sizable update and we're pushing a few more fixes and improvements your way… and - by popular demand - you can now customize your key bindings, keyboard players.

Concisely conveyed, we crafted a core capability called upon by our committed community keen on conquering critical combos courtesy of customizable controls (say that five times fast!).

We heard you loud and clear: you want to punch / slash / stab / club through the Wilds in your own way …

It turns out that implementing control remapping is a bit bigger than initially anticipated. Right now, the full implementation of control remapping will take awhile as we work to get the UI elements in place, but the core functionality of remapping is available. So we pulled forward custom keybinding work allowing players to edit a file to customize mouse-and-keyboard controls to their liking.

Is it pretty? Nope. Does it work? Absolutely.

So, our first step is to allow players to customize via an .ini file while we continue to work on the implementation of in-game remapping for both mouse-and-keyboard and controller.

General Fixes / Updates
Fixed an issue that caused other Aces to slide around on the World Map.
Fixed an issue where the McKrakenstein and Iron Pox Masks names and descriptions were swapped in the Nightcloak’s Vault.
Combat: Fixed an issue that caused the Ace to ignore HitStop during attacks after being hit by an Environmental Hazard.
Combat: Fixed an issue where it was too easy to do infinite combos to airborne enemies with the Sentinel Class. You can still juggle enemies for quite awhile but they’ll eventually fall to the ground faster if you don’t mix up your combo enough.

[hr][/hr]
How to Remap Key Bindings

Just to be clear, this isn’t the final solution. And, as soon as you get really good at this process - we encourage you to quickly forget it. Because, we’re going to put out a nice, shiny, user interface for remapping controls. Until then, you'll find a step-by-step instruction video below, with each step detailed beneath it. Enjoy remapping your controls!

[previewyoutube=WRqfbw3YVas;full][/previewyoutube]

Step 1
Grab a Founder’s Pack - and Download Towerborne :)

Step 2
Click on Towerborne in Steam so that the main game page is displayed with the Play button.

Step 3
Click on the Manage button on the right side of the Play button.
Highlight Manage and select Browse Local Files. This will open the folder where Towerborne is installed.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44237228/0edcc455ce0f652077d5981a81d8e0628f4bba91.png
Step 4
Now that you’re in the Towerborne folder, double click on the Belfry folder.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44237228/f0e491da240b1531c5486f50be4b9e222197bf02.png

Step 5
While inside the Belfry folder, right click and select New -> Folder. 
Name this folder “Config”.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44237228/78ffec0f0a1f10c6686cdaf914ca70e376663cef.gif

Step 6
Open the “Config” folder that you just created.

While inside the Config folder, right click and select New -> Text Document. 
Name this document “UserInput.ini”.

You will get a confirmation message asking if you want to change the extension of the file. 
Hit “Yes”.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44237228/6b7ee3b0ed977a2b3be852ec48c801b7523f6177.gif

If you don’t have Show File Extensions enabled, the above steps will not work. However, you can still create the .ini file by following similar steps.

1. Right Click -> Create New Text Document
2. Open the text document
3. Go to File -> Save As
4. Make sure the directory you're saving to is Towerborne -> Belfry -> Config
5. Under filename type “UserInput.ini” without quotations
6. In the Save as type select “All files”

This process should create the UserInput.ini file.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44237228/a772f41b07800e3126dac6ebb8780143214c99df.gif

Step 7
Double click on the new “UserInput.ini” file that you just created. This should open up your default text editing software.

Step 8
Copy and Paste the following text into UserInput.ini. These are the game’s default controls.

[code][/Script/BfInput.BfEnhancedPlayerInput]
+MappingOverrides=(InputMapName="Up",InputKeyName="W")
+MappingOverrides=(InputMapName="Down",InputKeyName="S")
+MappingOverrides=(InputMapName="Left",InputKeyName="A")
+MappingOverrides=(InputMapName="Right",InputKeyName="D")
+MappingOverrides=(InputMapName="Jump",InputKeyName="SpaceBar")
+MappingOverrides=(InputMapName="LightAttack",InputKeyName="LeftMouseButton")
+MappingOverrides=(InputMapName="HeavyAttack",InputKeyName="RightMouseButton")
+MappingOverrides=(InputMapName="Evade",InputKeyName="MiddleMouseButton")
+MappingOverrides=(InputMapName="FocusSkillShift",InputKeyName="LeftShift")
+MappingOverrides=(InputMapName="Umbra",InputKeyName="LeftControl")
+MappingOverrides=(InputMapName="SocialWheel",InputKeyName="Three")
+MappingOverrides=(InputMapName="Interact",InputKeyName="E")
+MappingOverrides=(InputMapName="FocusSkillLight",InputKeyName="X")
+MappingOverrides=(InputMapName="FocusSkillHeavy",InputKeyName="C")
+MappingOverrides=(InputMapName="ClassMechanic",InputKeyName="LeftAlt")
[/code]
The InputMapName is largely self-explanatory. The Ace’s movement directions are Up, Down, Left, Right.

FocusSkillShift represents the modifier button for doing Focus Skills. If you hold this button and then press Light or Heavy Attack, you will do a Light or Heavy Focus Skill.

FocusSkillLight and FocusSkillHeavy provide alternative button mappings so that you can just press a single button to perform those specific actions. No need to even use the FocusSkillShift key. It’s not displayed anywhere in the game, but with default controls this is already assigned to X and C. It’s also assigned to I and O by default if you’re just using Keyboard Controls.

Step 9
To change your controls, change the “InputKeyName” section to the Keybind of your choice. 
For example, if you want Evade to be mapped to Left Shift, it would look like this:

[code]+MappingOverrides=(InputMapName="Evade",InputKeyName="LeftShift")
[/code]
Step 10
Once you’re done making your modifications, save the UserInput.ini file.

Step 11
Now you’re ready to play the game! Once you load the game, your new control scheme should just work. Since these changes are being made in an .ini file, you cannot make changes while the game is running. Sorry.

It’s also worth noting that you will not see your new keys displayed in-game. This will work once the full feature is released, but for now the inputs you see on screen will not be reflective of your changes.

Examples of Keybind Remapping
If you wanted to create a control scheme that utilized the Arrow Keys for movement and combat actions on the left side of the keyboard, it would look something like this:

[code][/Script/BfInput.BfEnhancedPlayerInput]
+MappingOverrides=(InputMapName="Up",InputKeyName="Up")
+MappingOverrides=(InputMapName="Down",InputKeyName="Down")
+MappingOverrides=(InputMapName="Left",InputKeyName="Left")
+MappingOverrides=(InputMapName="Right",InputKeyName="Right")
+MappingOverrides=(InputMapName="Jump",InputKeyName="SpaceBar")
+MappingOverrides=(InputMapName="LightAttack",InputKeyName="A")
+MappingOverrides=(InputMapName="HeavyAttack",InputKeyName="S")
+MappingOverrides=(InputMapName="Evade",InputKeyName="D")
+MappingOverrides=(InputMapName="Umbra",InputKeyName="Q")
+MappingOverrides=(InputMapName="SocialWheel",InputKeyName="Three")
+MappingOverrides=(InputMapName="Interact",InputKeyName="F")
+MappingOverrides=(InputMapName="FocusSkillLight",InputKeyName="W")
+MappingOverrides=(InputMapName="FocusSkillHeavy",InputKeyName="E")
+MappingOverrides=(InputMapName="ClassMechanic",InputKeyName="R")
[/code]
If you wanted to create a modified version of the existing control scheme where you moved the Evade button to LeftShift, Umbra to MiddleMouseButton, ClassMechanic to C, Interact to F, and Light and Heavy Focus Skills to Q and E, it would look something like this:

[code][/Script/BfInput.BfEnhancedPlayerInput]
+MappingOverrides=(InputMapName="Up",InputKeyName="W")
+MappingOverrides=(InputMapName="Down",InputKeyName="S")
+MappingOverrides=(InputMapName="Left",InputKeyName="A")
+MappingOverrides=(InputMapName="Right",InputKeyName="D")
+MappingOverrides=(InputMapName="Jump",InputKeyName="SpaceBar")
+MappingOverrides=(InputMapName="LightAttack",InputKeyName="LeftMouseButton")
+MappingOverrides=(InputMapName="HeavyAttack",InputKeyName="RightMouseButton")
+MappingOverrides=(InputMapName="Evade",InputKeyName="LeftShift")
+MappingOverrides=(InputMapName="Umbra",InputKeyName="MiddleMouseButton")
+MappingOverrides=(InputMapName="SocialWheel",InputKeyName="Three")
+MappingOverrides=(InputMapName="Interact",InputKeyName="F")
+MappingOverrides=(InputMapName="FocusSkillLight",InputKeyName="Q")
+MappingOverrides=(InputMapName="FocusSkillHeavy",InputKeyName="E")
+MappingOverrides=(InputMapName="ClassMechanic",InputKeyName="C")
[/code]
Troubleshooting
If you ever run into a problem where your controls are not working as expected, you can revert back to the default control scheme by just deleting the UserInput.ini file. If you’re having issues with certain keys not working, please see the list of Valid Keys in the next section below and make sure that your spelling is exactly as written in this list.
